purpose: Caches content_url() results in per-blog_id static arrays inside the CSS and JS minifier classes (constructor + update_image_paths) to avoid re-invoking WordPress content_url() hooks in high-frequency minification paths.
riskRationale: The change is behavior-preserving (output is identical); blog_id keying correctly handles multisite switch_to_blog() as required by AGENTS.md. Main concerns are maintainability (three duplicated copies of the boilerplate) and a dubious performance premise, not broken functionality or security.

text: A logically-correct micro-optimization: content_url() calls in the CSS/JS minifier constructors and update_image_paths are cached in static arrays keyed by get_current_blog_id(), matching an existing pattern in class-main.php. However the benefit is largely theoretical because WordPress core's own content_url() already caches the filtered base URL in a static per request, and the new code duplicates a boilerplate pattern three times without the has_filter() gate that the pre-existing implementation uses.

reasoning: No bugs or security issues, but the newly-introduced caching boilerplate is duplicated across three sites and omits the has_filter('content_url') guard already established in class-main.php, adding unconditional branching overhead while the actual performance win is negligible. Consolidate into a shared helper and gate it consistently.

message: Blog_id keying of the static cache correctly mirrors the multisite-safe pattern required by AGENTS.md (transient/option isolation) and is consistent with the existing implementation in class-main.php, so switch_to_blog() lookups resolve to the right site.

The change is strictly behavior-preserving: $this->cache_url and $css_dir_url end up with identical values as before, just retrieved from a cache. Array-index spacing and static declarations are WPCS-conformant.

The same static-caching boilerplate is now duplicated in three places (class-css.php constructor line 82-100, class-css.php update_image_paths line 197-207, class-js.php constructor line 91-109), and it does NOT apply the has_filter('content_url') guard that the pre-existing implementation in class-main.php:2108-2118 uses before caching. This both adds maintainability debt (three copies to keep in sync) and runs the cache branches unconditionally, even when no content_url filter exists — which is precisely the case where the pre-existing code intentionally skips caching to avoid overhead.
suggestion: Extract a single shared helper, e.g. Util::cached_content_url( $path ), that keys a static array by blog_id and centralizes the pattern, then call it from both constructors and update_image_paths. Match the class-main.php convention of only caching when has_filter('content_url') is active, or at least single-source the logic to keep all call sites consistent.

message: The stated premise — that content_url() 'executes WP hooks for every replaced asset' — is inaccurate: WordPress core's content_url() already caches its filtered base URL in an internal static variable, so the content_url filter runs at most once per request regardless. The per-call cost is only path string substitution. Combined with the missing has_filter() gate above, the measurable benefit of this PR is likely negligible, and it adds complexity that would ideally be justified by before/after profiling.
suggestion: Profile (e.g. microtime across a page load with many inlined scripts/styles) to confirm the improvement is real and non-negligible; if it is, keep it but centralize the logic. If not, consider reverting to avoid YAGNI complexity.

message: The static array mixes the string sentinel key 'root' with per-path keys derived from str_replace(). Although path keys always begin with a leading '/' (so a literal 'root' collision is practically impossible), mixing a magic sentinel and computed keys in one array is fragile and easy to break in a future edit (e.g. if a cache path ever resolves to bare 'root').
suggestion: Use a distinct key namespace for the root case (e.g. $cache_url[$blog_id]['__root__']) or compute the root via the shared helper path so the array holds only uniform relative-path keys.

suggestion: Remove the duplicate entry, or give the 2026-08-04 entry distinct content that reflects what was actually changed this time (e.g. extending the cache to update_image_paths and the JS constructor).
